description: The COMPLETE state of an agent graph at one moment: the nodes (agents, tools, resources, the human), the connections between them and the call counts each connection carried — plus the Sequence the snapshot includes. A snapshot is what a graph surface renders; it never polls and never mutates. A deep link, a reload and the repair after a gap all produce a new snapshot and the surface simply draws it, which is why Apply returns a NEW value instead of editing this one. Both lists may be empty and a null list is normalised to an empty one, so a component never has to null-check the host's data.

members.name: Sequence
members.description: The sequence this snapshot includes — the baseline an event stream starts from. Zero (the default) means the host does not track sequences for snapshots, which is legal: the stream then starts without a baseline and accepts the run's first event.

members.name: Nodes
members.description: The nodes of the graph, in the order the layout starts from. Empty is legal (an empty graph).

members.name: Edges
members.description: The connections between nodes, in any order. An edge naming a node the snapshot does not contain is COUNTED by the layout and never drawn, because its geometry would be a guess.

members.name: Apply
members.description: Folds an incremental batch of calls into this snapshot and returns the result as a NEW value; this instance is never modified. Each call ADDS its Count to the addressed edge, marks it active and moves its LastCallAt forward (never back). A call naming an edge the snapshot does not have is ignored, because an edge cannot be invented from one endpoint pair. A batch that changes nothing returns THIS instance, so a host can compare by reference.
